speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. Please describe exactly what your double vision looks like, such as whether the images move in opposite directions or if one eye is misaligned, and tell me if your symptoms worsen during the day. Also, can you clarify which upper limb muscles are weak and how your difficulty climbing stairs compares to your previous ability?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. Your symptoms of diplopia triggered by vertical gaze, worsening with activity (fatigability), and proximal limb weakness without sensory or balance deficits are classic for this neuromuscular junction disorder. I recommend requesting a Tensilon (Edrophonium) test and checking acetylcholine receptor antibodies to confirm.
